note: The Credit Reporting Act, 2007 (Act 726), as amended by the Data Protection Act, 2012, in Parliament of Ghana's repository copy (ir.parliament.gh, which doesn't answer this environment), read from archive.org's snapshot of 14 December 2024. Section 24(3)(b): a financial institution gives licensed credit bureaus monthly the status of performance of the customer's obligations under each credit agreement, with no threshold: written as reported 30 days after the due date (a monthly cycle). Section 30(2): a credit bureau keeps information in its database for a maximum of six years from the occurrence of the basis for keeping it (ten years for a criminal conviction): written as keep six years. Section 25 lets a lender report loans 90 days past due without the customer's consent, after 28 days' notice; the form holds one reporting rule and uses the monthly one. The Credit Reporting Regulations, 2020 (L.I. 2394), on the Bank of Ghana's site and read by eye, also have monthly updates by the 15th (reg. 4) and set no other retention period; no later amendment to section 30 was found (the Bank of Ghana's media library holds the 2020 Regulations and the bureaus' annual reports, none amending it).

sources.said: A financial institution shall on a monthly basis provide information to licensed credit bureaus on the status of performance of the customer's obligations under the credit agreement or facility. ... Section 30—Retention period of credit information database ... (2) A credit bureau shall maintain information in its database for (a) a maximum period of six years from the occurrence of the basis for keeping the information on record, or (b) a period of ten years in the case of a criminal conviction.
